name: mirador
description: A canvas for your coding agent. It draws what it means, asks you with pictures, and walks you through its changes and reviews, right beside the conversation. Desktop app for macOS and Linux.

paragraphs: Mirador runs your coding agents (Claude Code and opencode) and gives them a canvas beside the conversation. On the canvas they draw what they mean, ask you with pictures, walk you through code, and hand you code reviews you can walk through. It runs on your own computer, with your own agent settings.
That installs the desktop app on a Mac with Apple Silicon, or on Linux (x64 or arm64), and starts it. It runs the Claude Code or opencode you already have. More ways to get it.
A mirador is a lookout: the place you climb to see the whole landscape at once.
features: It shows you what it means: architecture, flows, data, mockups, charts, even 3D scenes, instead of describing them.
It asks you with pictures: two to eight options, each with a preview, and you click one.
It walks you through code: how something works, or what it just changed, as a tour of the code in the order it runs, with the changed lines marked.
It hands you a review to walk through: the change as a guided tour of the code in the order it runs, with findings pinned to the lines they are about, ready to post to the pull request.

whatItDoes.text: Mirador runs your coding agents (Claude Code and opencode) and gives them a canvas beside the conversation. On the canvas they draw what they mean, ask you with pictures, walk you through code, and hand you code reviews you can walk through. It runs on your own computer, with your own agent settings.

requirements.text: Signing in: Mirador runs the claude on your PATH (or in /.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin), or the program set in Settings › Agents, so it uses the sign-in and version you already have.
Without a sign-in, a conversation offers Log in, which opens that Claude Code's own sign-in in a terminal tab.
